note: Safety lines the advice classifier (rule-checks.mjs safetyTopics: an instruction plus a word-list topic) does not catch, added by reading every bank line that mentions a storm, lightning, hail, wind, fog, driving, sun, heat, water or staying inside. A safety line is one that tells the reader to do or not do something protective. Al's brief: safety lines must pass both back-translations (and SSA-COMET for isiZulu) or show in English. Jokes that only mention the weather, and clothing advice, are not on the list.

lines.en: Don't even think about driving somewhere.
Stay safe. The sky is making a point.
Unplug the things. The sky has plans.
Wait it out indoors. The mountains aren't going anywhere.
Unplug the TV — it's tradition.
Thunder rolling in. Inside is the move.
Lightning's putting on a show — watch from the window.
Tiny ice bombs falling. Indoors is the only plan.
Windows closed, kettle on, and wait.
Sky's grumbling. Stay close to a roof.
Let's call it atmosphere and go inside.
Nobody is driving home in this. That's not laziness, that's science.
Driving slow is not a suggestion.
SPF 50 or regret it by tonight.
Your future self will thank you for that sunscreen.
You will look like a lobster. You've been warned.
Wind's on the cards. Peg the washing down.
Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
Hold your hat. Hold your kid. Just hold on.
Close it, tie it down, surrender.
Water consumption: yes. All of it.
Move slowly. Speak slowly. Survive.
The water looks like glass. It feels like ice. Do not run the experiment.
